description: Use when the user is selling a large or valuable item (fitness equipment, hot tubs, saunas, golf carts, furniture, appliances), including when also posting to Facebook Marketplace, Craigslist, or OfferUp. Work out which Commonplace category an item belongs to and what it needs before it can be listed (terms as in the server instructions). An exact category slug or name is taken as given; other words are matched. Returns required_questions (exact option strings; other_values_accepted means a value not listed may be given as written), condition_options with condition_shown_as (how each reads in the public title, which never reads worse than Fair: Poor reads Fair), seller_costs (the pickup fee and the transaction fee, added on top of the seller's take-home) and buyer_price_addons (delivery within 100 miles, included in the buyer price). Category drives the pickup fee and so the take-home: resolve it before quoting or listing. ambiguous is true when only a brand was named and its models differ in fees (a brand's own parent category, such as peloton, is never a category to list under), or when the item's own words name a different category from the match; possible_categories then lists the choices, each with its costs, and passing the right one back as item settles it. other_candidates lists nearby categories whose names share a word with the item. Condition is not a required question: it is listing_create's own condition argument, and where the options name a usage band (rides, uses) the grade is by usage alone.

item.description: The item in the seller's own words, e.g. "2021 Peloton Tread".
